First, we want to find the interval for $\theta $ that corresponds to the first petal. Since the curve bounding the region crosses itself at the origin, we want to find the values of $\theta $ for which $r=0$, or 

$$
4\operatorname{cos}⁡(4\theta )=0.
$$

This gives us two solutions for $4\theta \in [-\pi ,\pi ):$

$$
4\theta =-\frac{\pi }{2},\frac{\pi }{2}\,⟹\,\theta =-\frac{\pi }{8},\frac{\pi }{8}
$$

As a result, the first petal is traversed for $-\frac{\pi }{8}\le \theta \le \frac{\pi }{8}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14226336/assets/e1f3651f2c120b65063015a17a7e657ccb5b2e87df475660785d35748c05557a.png)

Since there are $8$ petals, the total area bounded by the polar curve can be calculated as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{\text{total}} & =8\cdot {A}_{\text{petal}} \\  & =8\cdot \frac{1}{2}{\int }_{-\pi /8}^{\pi /8}{(4\operatorname{cos}⁡(4\theta ))}^{2}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =8\cdot \frac{16}{2}{\int }_{-\pi /8}^{\pi /8}{cos}^{2}⁡(4\theta )\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =64\cdot \frac{1}{2}{\int }_{-\pi /8}^{\pi /8}(1+\operatorname{cos}⁡(8\theta ))\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =32{(\theta +\frac{1}{8}\operatorname{sin}⁡(8\theta ))|}_{-\pi /8}^{\pi /8} \\  & =32[(\frac{\pi }{8}+\frac{1}{8}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi ))-(-\frac{\pi }{8}+\frac{1}{8}\operatorname{sin}⁡(-\pi ))] \\  & =32(\frac{\pi }{8}+\frac{\pi }{8}) \\  & =8\pi \end{aligned}
$$
